checks.name: Stock markets
checks.question: Are most of the big stock markets rising?

week.reading: 0 of 6 stock markets up, 5 down, 1 flat

checks.name: Fear gauges
checks.question: Are the market fear gauges (VIX) falling? They rise when investors get nervous.

week.reading: 1 of 2 fear gauges up, 0 down, 1 flat

month.reading: 1 of 2 fear gauges up, 0 down, 1 flat

checks.name: US dollar
checks.question: Is the US dollar weakening? Investors tend to buy dollars when they feel unsafe.

checks.name: Junk bonds versus government bonds
checks.question: Are riskier company bonds doing better than safe government bonds?

week.reading: Government bonds did better than junk bonds

month.reading: Junk bonds and government bonds did about the same

checks.name: Growth sectors versus defensive sectors
checks.question: Are sectors that need a strong economy (consumer, industrial, materials) doing better than steady ones (food, utilities, healthcare)?

week.reading: Defensive sectors did better than growth-linked sectors

month.reading: Defensive sectors did better than growth-linked sectors

checks.name: Small companies versus large companies
checks.question: Are small companies doing better than large ones? Small companies tend to lead when investors are confident.

week.reading: Small companies and large companies did about the same

month.reading: Small companies and large companies did about the same

checks.name: Copper versus gold
checks.question: Is copper (needed by factories) doing better than gold (a safe place to park money)?

week.reading: Copper and gold did about the same

regime.method: 8 simple checks look at groups of markets over the last week and the last month. Each check votes risk-on (investors look comfortable owning riskier things), risk-off (investors look defensive) or neutral. The banner says risk-on or risk-off only when at least 60% of the checks that have data lean the same way and no more than 1 leans the other way; otherwise it says mixed.
regime.notice: A plain checklist of market groups, for research. It describes how markets behaved over the last week and month. It does not predict what comes next and it is not investment advice. No model chooses this label.

executive_summary.headline: Outflows dominate global equities and commodities across weekly and monthly windows despite daily trend improvements, as market sentiment maintains a firm risk-off posture overall.
executive_summary.rotation_view: Across the month and week, money flows show widespread outflows across Country and regional markets, Size and style, Metals, and Crypto. S&P 500, Semiconductors, and Bitcoin face sustained selling pressure, though Indian equity proxies like Nifty 50 ETF (NIFTYBEES) attract gains. Broad market participation remains negative across short and medium horizons despite minor day-level stabilization. The risk tone is risk-off across both weekly and monthly measures.
executive_summary.drivers_view: Press coverage focuses heavily on executive leadership updates and market reactions surrounding Nvidia, alongside analyst commentary on memory chip supply impacting Micron. In official macro data, Federal Reserve total assets, US 2-year Treasury yield, and US 10-year Treasury yield moved down, while US M2 money stock rose.
